# Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice

## Original exercise

James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
\(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).

> 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
> prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.

## Definitions and complete target

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

value.representation_notes: V is an arbitrary complex vector space and x,y,h are its complex-linear Chevalley actions. H003 retains finite dimension, all three commutators, a highest vector of weight λ and irreducibility under the generating actions; this is the operator presentation of the given sl₂-module, with the specified v retained separately in H004. λ remains an integer. Under H002, Index λ = Fin(λ.toNat+1) identifies bijectively with {i∈ℤ | 0≤i≤λ}; natural differences are used only inside this range. M is a ℤ-submodule of V; H005 supplies an arbitrary integer basis that is also a complex basis, and stability under every divided power. R is the ℤ-subalgebra of ℚ generated by the displayed prime-to-p fractions, with its exact original carrier established by T005; it is not assumed to be the whole ℚ. MR=R⊗ℤM and iota is the actual scalar multiplication lift; identifying with its image is justified only by N002. J_i and J are preimages of that image under c↦c e_i. qmul is the actual multiplication map ℚ⊗R J→ℂ. Scalar-first VK=K⊗ℤM is the same source tensor construction with factors swapped; T014 uses this convention throughout. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the image of multiplication by p. LatticeOps carries the actual restrictions, and Agrees specifies each value, rather than adding any action assumption. The target constructs these unique restrictions and states nonzero VK and every K-submodule invariant under x,y,h is bottom or top. Proposition-valued definitions only package displayed obligations; none proves them. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, integer coefficients are cast to the indicated field, and all factorials/choose arguments are natural numbers. Inspected pinned APIs: CharP K p asserts exactly (n:K)=0 iff p divides n, rather than merely p·1=0. Module.End multiplication is f.comp g, and Basis.coord is the coefficient function from its finitely-supported coordinate equivalence. LinearMap.liftBaseChange sends s⊗m to s•f(m), while LinearMap.baseChange sends s⊗m to s⊗f(m). ModN is the quotient by the range of the integer-linear p-multiplication map and its ZMod-module instance is canonical. ZMod.algebra is explicitly installed under CharP; the R-action on K is explicitly the one supplied by κ.toAlgebra. Scalar towers for R⊂ℚ⊂ℂ and R⊂ℂ acting on V use those actual inclusion maps. The two finrank theorems require strong rank condition; here R is a subring of ℚ and ℚ is a field, so these are consequences, not extra parameters.

steps.statement: Lowering lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Simultaneous natural induction using the three commutators. Natural t and t+1 encode the source nonnegative and positive integer powers.

steps.statement: ∀ i : Index lam, e y v i.val ≠ 0 ∧ h (e y v i.val) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • e y v i.val)
steps.explanation: Iterate the x identity, obtaining i! times the descending product; all factors are nonzero over ℂ for i≤λ. Divide by i! and retain the weight formula.

steps.statement: CoordinateCore lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Isolate coefficients by products of h minus the other complex weights, use dimension to obtain the e basis, exclude the additional weight −λ−2, and derive terminated generator strings. No reduced-weight assertion is used.

steps.statement: Coordinates lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Export all of N001, including the count, lowering identities, nonzero vectors, basis, termination, and integral binomial divided-power formulas. Iterate the generator formulas and use zero-extended families at the ends.

steps.statement: (∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ localRing p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)) ∧ IsFractionRing (R p) ℚ
steps.explanation: Representation bridge for D007: the displayed fractions are closed under ring operations when p is prime, so their ℤ-adjoin has exactly that carrier. Since it contains ℤ and embeds in ℚ, ℚ is its fraction field. This establishes the concrete localization meaning before using its denominators.

steps.statement: LocalLattice p lam M x y h
steps.explanation: Extend an arbitrary admissible integer basis to R; compare its image in V to prove iota injective, free rank n, and full complex span. Use stability under divided powers and h=xy−yx; construct, rather than assume, the integer lattice restrictions LatticeOps.

steps.statement: LocalLattice p lam M x y h ∧ MatrixIdentities p lam M x y v
steps.explanation: Export N002. Evaluate Pi and the two edge products on the e basis. Use λ

steps.statement: ∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v
steps.explanation: Matrix units transport c e_j to c e_i; reverse i,j to prove equality. The zero index is present because H002 identifies Fin(λ.toNat+1) with the source interval.

steps.statement: CommonModule p lam M y v
steps.explanation: Export N003. The finite sum of J coordinates gives the displayed R-linear isomorphism with MR, using iota injectivity and the complex e basis. Diagonal images of finitely many generators make J finite; full span makes it nonzero.

steps.statement: Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧ (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧ Module.Finite ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v)
steps.explanation: Clear a common nonzero denominator in a finite tensor sum. Its image is c/d, so vanishing forces c=0. Finite generation of J yields finite-dimensional rational scalar extension.

steps.statement: RationalLine p M y v
steps.explanation: Tensor the explicit coordinate isomorphism with ℚ. Use Module.finrank_baseChange on MR and Module.finrank_pi_fintype on the finite constant family QJ directly, with the actual freeness/finiteness conditions, to obtain n=nr and hence r=1. The balanced coordinate inverse avoids a flatness assumption.

steps.statement: ∃ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b
steps.explanation: Choose a nonzero rational-line vector and finitely many nonzero generators. Write each rational coefficient as p^eta times a unit of R and choose the minimum exponent. Prove both inclusions J=Rb; no PID shortcut replaces this supplied argument.

steps.statement: PrincipalLattice p lam M y v
steps.explanation: Export N004, including rational multiplication injectivity, rational span and rank one, existence of b, and an R-basis for every nonzero b generating J. Construct the basis using the common-module coordinate isomorphism.

steps.statement: ScalarReduction p K M
steps.explanation: Construct κ by fractions, then the two canonical scalar-first tensor isomorphisms by the source pure-tensor formulas and their inverses. ModN(MR,p) is literally MR/pMR and has its canonical ZMod p action. Prove naturality for lattice endomorphisms; the intermediate R and ZMod algebra structures are supplied explicitly inside TensorMaps.

steps.statement: ReducedBasis p lam K M x y h v
steps.explanation: Choose b from N004, scalar-extend its R-basis, and pull it back through the natural tensor isomorphism. Keep the exact basis/image equation, then transfer the integer generator matrices and dimension.

steps.statement: ScalarReduction p K M ∧ ReducedBasis p lam K M x y h v ∧ ReducedUnits lam K M x y h ∧ ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a
steps.explanation: Export N005. Prove all factorials through λ and all relevant binomials nonzero in K. Extend r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r, reduce the original matrix-unit identity through the same scaled basis, and obtain the delta action. Indices are natural differences guarded by i,j≤λ. Its delta formula is stated for every basis with the generator formulas, so the very same beta exported by ReducedBasis satisfies all N005 assertions.

steps.statement: ∀ (a : LatticeOps M) (W : Submodule K (VK K M)), Agrees M x y h a → Invariant W (a.x.baseChange K) → Invariant W (a.y.baseChange K) → Invariant W (a.h.baseChange K) → ∀ i j : Index lam, Invariant W (MatrixWord lam (fun r => (a.X r).baseChange K) (fun r => (a.Y r).baseChange K) i j)
steps.explanation: Powers of preserving x,y preserve W. For every index in MatrixWord, N005 identifies the divided powers with scalar multiples of those powers; scalar multiplication and composition preserve W.

steps.statement: ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a → Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)
steps.explanation: Use the N005 beta basis and separate zero/nonzero W. In the nonzero case choose a single compatible vector, coefficient family, and nonzero coordinate; apply the matrix word and divide to put every beta_i in W. Basis cardinality λ.toNat+1 supplies nontriviality. All temporary witnesses remain local.

steps.statement: Target K M x y h
steps.explanation: Choose the actual lattice restrictions carried with N005 and apply T018. These are N002's already constructed restrictions transported through N005, not an additional original premise. Agrees pins their values uniquely on M. Nontriviality and the zero/top invariant-subspace alternative are the complete target; invariance under the three Chevalley generators is equivalent to invariance under their K-span, including characteristic two.

R001.fact: In a finite-dimensional vector space W over a field, a linearly independent family indexed by a finite set J with |J|=dim W is a basis.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space of finite dimension λ+1.
F001 gives |I|=n=λ+1.
Before the dimension step, the displayed polynomial calculation proves linear independence of (e_i).

R001.justification: The elementary exchange argument bounds the size of any independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: insert independent vectors successively into a spanning list, each time replacing a vector with nonzero coefficient in an expansion, preserving spanning. If an independent family of size dim W did not span, adjoining a vector outside its span would give an independent family of size dim W+1, contradicting that bound applied to a basis of W. Thus the given family spans and is a basis.

R001.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m!/(r!(m−r)!) is an integer, denoted binom(m,r). Consequently, for integers a≥0 and r≥0, (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer, with empty product 1.

grounds.reason: λ is a nonnegative integer.
i∈I means 0≤i≤λ, so both a=λ−i and a=i are nonnegative integers.
r is an arbitrary natural number.
The two computed successive products use a=λ−i and a=i, respectively.

R001.justification: The factorial quotients equal 1 at r=0 and r=m. For 0<r<m, direct common-denominator arithmetic gives C(m,r)=C(m−1,r−1)+C(m−1,r). Induction on m therefore proves every such quotient integral. Cancelling a! in (a+r)!/a! gives the stated successive-product expression. Interpreting these integers in ℂ gives exactly the coefficients in S005; all factorial denominators are nonzero.

R002.fact: If (m_i) indexed by the finite set I is an integer basis of M and also a complex basis of V, then R⊗_ℤ M has R-basis (1⊗m_i). The map r⊗m↦rm into V is injective, has image the R-span of M, and its image spans V over ℂ. Here |I|=n, so its R-rank is n.

grounds.reason: H005 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V.
N001 supplies the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I and |I|=n, so finite-dimensional basis cardinality gives the same indexing size for m.
R is a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ under H001.
M_R is the stated tensor product.
iota is the canonical scalar-multiplication map.

R002.justification: Finite basis exchange gives equality of the cardinalities of the two complex bases. Write a_i:M→ℤ for the integer coordinate maps for m. The maps r⊗m↦r a_i(m) are well-defined by bilinearity and give an inverse to (r_i)↦∑r_i⊗m_i. The map into V sends this sum to ∑r_i m_i, which vanishes only if every coefficient vanishes, by complex independence and R⊂ℂ. Its image is precisely the finite R-linear combinations of M, contains each m_i, and hence has complex span V. This elaborates the coordinate construction already displayed in S001.

R002.fact: For a prime p and integers 0≤j≤λ<p, the integer c=binom(λ,j) is not divisible by p and is a unit in R=ℤ_(p), with inverse 1/c∈R.

grounds.reason: p is prime.
j∈I means 0≤j≤λ.
A rational with denominator not divisible by p belongs to R.
S002 uses the integer identity c j!(λ−j)!=λ!.

R002.justification: Each positive factor in these factorials is less than p and therefore coprime to p; the Euclidean algorithm gives an inverse for its residue modulo p. Products of these invertible residues remain invertible, including the empty product 1. Thus p does not divide λ!. If p divided c, the displayed integer identity would force p to divide λ!, a contradiction. Consequently c≠0 and the fraction 1/c satisfies the defining denominator condition for R; its product with c is 1.

R003.fact: For the R-module L=iota(M_R), the image E_ii(L)=J e_i is finitely generated: L has a finite generating family because M_R is free of finite rank n and iota is an R-linear isomorphism onto L. Moreover c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated.

grounds.reason: M_R is free of finite rank n and iota embeds it in V.
iota is R-linear.
F001 identifies E_ii(L) with J e_i.
Each e_i is a nonzero vector of a complex basis.
0≤λ gives 0∈I, so an index i can be taken, including when λ=0.

R003.justification: Choose a finite basis b_1,…,b_n of M_R from its finite freeness. Their images generate L. By R-linearity, E_ii(∑ r_a iota(b_a))=∑ r_a E_ii(iota(b_a)), so these finitely many projected images generate J e_i. Scalar multiplication J→J e_i is surjective by the definition of J e_i and injective since e_i≠0 in a complex vector space. Transporting the projected generators through its inverse yields a finite generating family of J.

R004.fact: For R=ℤ_(p)⊂ℚ and an R-submodule J⊂ℂ, every element of ℚ⊗_R J has the form d⁻¹⊗c with 0≠d∈R and c∈J. Multiplication is a well-defined injective ℚ-linear map with image span_ℚ(J). If J is finitely generated over R, the images of those generators span the tensor product over ℚ.

grounds.reason: p is prime, so D007 defines the stated subring.
R contains ℤ and is contained in ℚ.
J is an R-submodule of ℂ and finitely generated.

R004.justification: For a finite sum ∑ρ_j⊗c_j choose a common nonzero integer denominator d and integers a_j=dρ_j. Balancing gives ∑ρ_j⊗c_j=d⁻¹⊗∑a_jc_j. Multiplication is balanced because the R actions are scalar multiplication in ℂ. If its image is zero, c/d=0 in ℂ forces c=0. Its image consists precisely of rational linear combinations, and an R-generating expression for c gives the asserted finite rational spanning set.

R004.fact: For finite I and an R-linear isomorphism M_R≅∏_{i∈I}J, the map ℚ⊗_R M_R→∏_{i∈I}(ℚ⊗_R J) specified in S002 is a ℚ-linear isomorphism.

grounds.reason: I is finite of cardinal n.
iota identifies M_R with its image.
The specified finite coordinate map is an R-linear isomorphism.

R004.justification: After using that coordinate isomorphism, project each pure tensor to its component tensors. For the inverse, apply the tensor of each coordinate insertion to the corresponding tensor component and sum over finite I. The maps exist by balancing. Projection followed by insertion is the identity on the corresponding component and zero on all others; the sum of insertion-projection maps is the identity on the finite product. Checking on pure tensors therefore proves both compositions are identities. No exactness or flatness theorem is involved.

R004.fact: The rings R=ℤ_(p) and ℚ satisfy the strong rank condition. A finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space is free and finitely generated; finite dimension is invariant under linear isomorphism. A finite free R-module of rank n has natural finrank n, so the finite-rank uses of M001 and M002 here measure the ordinary dimensions appearing in S002.

grounds.reason: R is a subring of ℚ containing ℤ.
M_R is free of the finite rank n.
QJ is finite-dimensional.
n is finite and strictly positive.

R004.justification: A finite rational spanning set yields a basis by successively removing dependent vectors. Gaussian elimination shows an independent family in ℚ^t has size at most t, proving strong rank for ℚ and invariance of finite basis size. If an injective matrix R^s→R^t had a nonzero rational kernel vector, multiplying it by a common nonzero integer denominator would give a nonzero kernel vector in R^s. Its rational extension is thus injective, so s≤t. This proves strong rank for R; comparison of finite bases consequently identifies the rank and its natural conversion with n. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases.

R004.fact: In a one-dimensional ℚ-subspace of ℂ, every nonzero a spans the space, so each nonzero g has the form g=qa for a nonzero rational q. A nonzero finitely generated module has a finite nonempty generating tuple with all entries nonzero.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated.
Multiplication embeds QJ as the rational span of J.
That space has dimension one.

R004.justification: The single nonzero vector a is independent over ℚ and hence is a basis in dimension one; the coordinate of a nonzero g cannot be zero. Removing zero elements from a finite generating family preserves its span, and an empty remaining family would generate only the zero module, contrary to nonzeroness.

R004.fact: If p is prime and q∈ℚ is nonzero, then q=p^ηu for some η∈ℤ and u with both numerator and denominator prime to p; consequently u,u⁻¹∈ℤ_(p).

grounds.reason: p is prime, in particular p≥2.
Membership in R is specified by a denominator not divisible by p.
Each q_j is a nonzero rational.

R004.justification: Write q=m/d with nonzero integers m,d. Repeated division by p terminates because absolute values strictly decrease when divisible, giving m=p^αm₀ and d=p^βd₀ with α,β≥0 and p dividing neither m₀ nor d₀. Set η=α−β and u=m₀/d₀. The two denominators d₀,m₀ show that u and u⁻¹ lie in R. These powers are in ℚ⊂ℂ, so even negative exponents are defined and nonzero. The finite minimum argument and the two module inclusions are already proved in S004.

R005.fact: For modules over commutative rings, a balanced additive pure-tensor formula induces a unique additive map on the tensor product, and equality on pure tensors implies equality of maps. In the present maps, compatibility with the K factor makes the induced maps K-linear. Applying an additive lattice operator to the M factor commutes with these scalar maps; an R-linear operator on M_R also descends to M_R/pM_R and commutes with the quotient tensor maps.

grounds.reason: M_R is R tensor_Z M.
V_K is M tensor_Z K.
All specified lattice operators preserve M and M_R; E_ij preserves M_R.
The maps and kappa compatibility are given explicitly.
The quotient maps are given explicitly and multiples of p tensor to zero.

R005.justification: The tensor product is generated by pure tensors modulo additivity and balancing relations. The displayed formulas respect those relations, so descend uniquely; composites fixing the generators are identity maps. Acting on the module factor commutes with changing scalar factors. For an R-linear A, A(pu)=pA(u), giving a quotient operator and the same compatibility on quotient generators.

R005.fact: If (a_i) over the finite index set I is an R-basis of an R-module L and kappa:R->K is a unital ring map, then (a_i tensor 1) is a K-basis of L tensor_R K. Every R-linear identity between operators on L remains an identity after scalar extension, with R coefficients mapped by kappa.

grounds.reason: For the chosen b, a_i=b e_i is an R-basis of M_R.
F001 identifies M_R tensor_R K with V_K compatibly with lattice operators.
The proof explicitly extends the basis coordinate maps.
The R-linear restrictions of the matrix units and their identities on M_R are available.

R005.justification: Write u=sum_i c_i a_i; then u tensor d=sum_i a_i tensor kappa(c_i)d, proving spanning. Each coordinate functional L->R induces L tensor_R K->K and evaluates a_j tensor 1 to delta_ij, proving independence. Operator sums, compositions and scalar multiplication have these same operations on pure tensors, so preserve identities. This verifies the scalar-extension steps already displayed in S003-S004.

R005.fact: In a field K of prime characteristic p, an integer a has zero image exactly when p divides a. Hence if 0<=r<p, the integer r! has nonzero image in K, including 0!=1. A unital ring map R->K sends each unit of R to a unit of K, and therefore to a nonzero element.

grounds.reason: p is prime and char K=p.
0<=lambda<p, and the local index r lies between 0 and lambda.
Each binom(lambda,j) used is a unit in R.
kappa is shown to be a unital ring map extending the integer map.

R005.justification: Divide an integer by p; its image is the image of its remainder. By the defining minimal positive characteristic, no remainder from 1 through p-1 is zero, so the kernel is pZ. Every factor 1,...,r is consequently nonzero; a finite product of nonzero field elements is nonzero. For a unit t with inverse s, kappa(t)kappa(s)=1, so kappa(t) is invertible and cannot be zero in a field.

R006.fact: If W is a K-linear subspace of a K-vector space and A(W)⊆W, then A^r(W)⊆W for every natural r. Scalar multiples and compositions of W-preserving linear maps also preserve W.

grounds.reason: W is a K-linear subspace of V_K.
L1 assumes invariance under x,y,h.
The relevant divided powers are scalar multiples of powers of x,y, with nonzero factorial denominators.

R006.justification: A^0 is the identity; repeated application of preservation proves the claim for A^r. For w∈W, closure under K-scalars puts aA(w) in W, and B(w)∈W followed by A(B(w))∈W proves closure under composition. Apply these facts to the displayed finite product defining T_ij.

R006.fact: For a finite K-basis (beta_i) indexed by I and a K-linear subspace W≠{0}, there jointly exist w∈W, coefficients (c_i)∈K^I and j∈I such that w≠0, w=Σ_i c_i beta_i and c_j≠0.

grounds.reason: N005 provides the finite I-indexed K-basis.
beta is chosen as that basis and W is a K-linear subspace.
L3 is W≠{0} in this branch.
I is the finite integer interval from 0 to λ.

R006.justification: Every subspace contains zero, so if it contained no nonzero vector it would equal {0}. Choose a nonzero w. The spanning property of a finite basis supplies its coefficient family. If all coefficients vanished, the finite sum would be zero, contrary to w≠0; thus one index j has c_j≠0. The index and coefficients refer to this same chosen expansion.

R006.fact: A K-linear map A satisfies A(Σ_k c_k beta_k)=Σ_k c_k A(beta_k) for a finite family. A K-linear subspace containing every element of a basis equals the whole ambient vector space.

grounds.reason: T_ij is a K-linear endomorphism, as in N005.
F003 supplies a finite basis expansion.
The chosen beta is a K-basis and T_ij beta_k=δ_jk beta_i.
The proof establishes beta_i∈W for arbitrary i.

R006.justification: Repeated additivity and scalar compatibility give the finite-sum identity; substituting the exported matrix-unit values leaves precisely c_j beta_i. For the second claim, expand any ambient vector in the basis and use closure of W under scalar multiplication and finite addition. These justify the displayed steps without adding a matrix-unit premise.

R006.fact: A vector space of positive finite dimension is nonzero. For a K-linear action of a Lie algebra spanned over K by x,y,h, a K-linear subspace is invariant under the entire Lie algebra if and only if it is invariant under x,y,h.

grounds.reason: N005 supplies dim_K(V_K)=λ+1>0 and the induced lattice operators.
H003 supplies the Chevalley generators and their operator action.
L_K is the K-tensor extension of the lattice spanned by x,y,h, with its induced action.

R006.justification: The zero vector space has dimension zero, so positive dimension excludes it. Each tensor of a lattice element ax+by+ch expands into a K-linear combination of the three tensor generators, and sums of such tensors span L_K. Linearity of the action and subspace closure show that preservation by the three generators implies preservation by every such combination. The converse follows by taking the generators themselves.

source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. Tensoring the integer coordinate isomorphism with R gives R-coordinates on M_R: finite sums ∑_{i∈I}r_i⊗m_i have unique coefficients r_i∈R. Explicitly the coordinate homomorphisms of M extend to these coordinates, and the sum map is their inverse. Under iota these basis tensors go to m_i, still complex-linearly independent, so iota is injective. This proves freeness of rank n and shows its image spans V over ℂ. Admissibility H005 gives preservation of M by every X_r,Y_r; extension by R gives preservation of M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve them; h=xy−yx by H003 preserves them too.

Fix i,j∈I. Evaluate using N001. X_λ kills e_k for k<λ and takes e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Therefore Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ. Also X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ. In Pi Y_(λ−j), an input e_k with kj goes past the end and is zero. At k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,j); hence Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ

Compose the identities F002. On the e basis, E_iλ E_λj=E_ij; thus E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002. Consequently E_ij preserves M_R for all i,j. Together with F001 and F002 these are the asserted lattice and matrix-unit identities. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. The image of such an expression is c0/d0; a zero image implies c0=0 and hence a zero tensor. Thus multiplication is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (gamma_i), the map sends ρ⊗(∑_{i∈I}gamma_i e_i) to (ρ⊗gamma_i)_{i∈I}; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

By H001, every integer prime to p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. The formula defining kappa:R→K is independent of fractional representatives by cross multiplication, preserves addition and multiplication, and extends the integer map. The balanced tensor maps V_K=M⊗_ℤ K→M_R⊗_R K and back are m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c and (s⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗kappa(s)c. The tensor relations show that both are well-defined; the two composites fix pure tensors, hence are identity maps. Thus they are inverse K-linear isomorphisms. Since the maps act only on scalar factors, they intertwine every operator preserving M, including x,y,h,X_r,Y_r by N002.

The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module. The maps M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K and back send u⊗c to [u]⊗c and [u]⊗c to u⊗c. Changing u by a multiple of p changes u⊗c by zero, since p=0 in K. These formulas are balanced for the quotient R-action, are independent of representatives, and are inverse on pure tensors. They give the second K-linear isomorphism and commute with all induced lattice operators. Combine with F001 to obtain both tensor identifications asserted in the output.

Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb using N004. The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R by N004, using iota from N002. Define beta_i to be its reduced image in V_K through F001. Scalar extension of its coordinate maps gives a K-basis: every pure tensor has its finite coordinate expansion in beta_i, and the extended coordinate maps take beta_i to the corresponding coordinate unit vectors, proving independence. Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. Applying N001 to b e_i and using the tensor isomorphisms gives x beta_0=0, x beta_i=(λ−i+1)beta_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<λ, y beta_λ=0; h beta_i=(λ−2i)beta_i. All coefficients are the integer images in K. This proves the required basis and its generator matrices.
For each r∈I, r≤λ

Choose the basis beta supplied by N005 and define T by its displayed formula. Let W⊆V_K be any K-linear subspace. Assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. Closure under x,y implies closure under their nonnegative powers. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. A linear subspace is closed under scalar multiplication and compositions of preserving maps, so W is invariant under every T_ij.
In the zero case temporarily assume L2: W={0}. Then the desired disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately. Discharge L2 to obtain the implication for this case.

For the other case assume L3: W≠{0}. A nonzero subspace contains a nonzero vector, and the beta basis of N005 expands any such vector uniquely. Its coefficients cannot all be zero. Thus there exist a vector w∈W, a coefficient family c∈K^I and an index j∈I with w=∑_{k∈I}c_k beta_k, w≠0 and c_j≠0. Record this compatible joint existence before choosing the witnesses.

Choose compatible w,c,j as in F003. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit action of N005 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. By F001 this vector belongs to W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives beta_i∈W. This holds for every i; since beta is a K-basis, W=V_K. No chosen vector or coordinate is present in that conclusion. Discharge L3 to obtain: if W≠{0}, then W=V_K.

Classical case elimination on W={0} or W≠{0}, using F002 and F004, gives W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W: every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V_K. N005 also gives dim_K V_K=λ+1>0, so V_K is nonzero. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.
M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: a free abelian subgroup admitting an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice assumption is imposed.

Let A be a semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective linear map between finite free A-modules has source rank at most target rank), let B be a finite index type, and for each t∈B let C_t be an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure, free and finitely generated over A. Then finrank_A(∏_{t∈B} C_t)=∑_{t∈B} finrank_A(C_t). Here finrank is cardinal module rank converted to a natural number (zero if that cardinal is infinite).

R001.fact: In a finite-dimensional vector space W over a field, a linearly independent family indexed by a finite set J with |J|=dim W is a basis.

R001.justification: The elementary exchange argument bounds the size of any independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: insert independent vectors successively into a spanning list, each time replacing a vector with nonzero coefficient in an expansion, preserving spanning. If an independent family of size dim W did not span, adjoining a vector outside its span would give an independent family of size dim W+1, contradicting that bound applied to a basis of W. Thus the given family spans and is a basis.

R001.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m!/(r!(m−r)!) is an integer, denoted binom(m,r). Consequently, for integers a≥0 and r≥0, (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer, with empty product 1.

R001.justification: The factorial quotients equal 1 at r=0 and r=m. For 0<r<m, direct common-denominator arithmetic gives C(m,r)=C(m−1,r−1)+C(m−1,r). Induction on m therefore proves every such quotient integral. Cancelling a! in (a+r)!/a! gives the stated successive-product expression. Interpreting these integers in ℂ gives exactly the coefficients in S005; all factorial denominators are nonzero.

source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. Tensoring the integer coordinate isomorphism with R gives R-coordinates on M_R: finite sums ∑_{i∈I}r_i⊗m_i have unique coefficients r_i∈R. Explicitly the coordinate homomorphisms of M extend to these coordinates, and the sum map is their inverse. Under iota these basis tensors go to m_i, still complex-linearly independent, so iota is injective. This proves freeness of rank n and shows its image spans V over ℂ. Admissibility H005 gives preservation of M by every X_r,Y_r; extension by R gives preservation of M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve them; h=xy−yx by H003 preserves them too.

Fix i,j∈I. Evaluate using N001. X_λ kills e_k for k<λ and takes e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Therefore Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ. Also X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ. In Pi Y_(λ−j), an input e_k with kj goes past the end and is zero. At k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,j); hence Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ

Compose the identities F002. On the e basis, E_iλ E_λj=E_ij; thus E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002. Consequently E_ij preserves M_R for all i,j. Together with F001 and F002 these are the asserted lattice and matrix-unit identities. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. The image of such an expression is c0/d0; a zero image implies c0=0 and hence a zero tensor. Thus multiplication is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (gamma_i), the map sends ρ⊗(∑_{i∈I}gamma_i e_i) to (ρ⊗gamma_i)_{i∈I}; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

By H001, every integer prime to p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. The formula defining kappa:R→K is independent of fractional representatives by cross multiplication, preserves addition and multiplication, and extends the integer map. The balanced tensor maps V_K=M⊗_ℤ K→M_R⊗_R K and back are m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c and (s⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗kappa(s)c. The tensor relations show that both are well-defined; the two composites fix pure tensors, hence are identity maps. Thus they are inverse K-linear isomorphisms. Since the maps act only on scalar factors, they intertwine every operator preserving M, including x,y,h,X_r,Y_r by N002.

The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module. The maps M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K and back send u⊗c to [u]⊗c and [u]⊗c to u⊗c. Changing u by a multiple of p changes u⊗c by zero, since p=0 in K. These formulas are balanced for the quotient R-action, are independent of representatives, and are inverse on pure tensors. They give the second K-linear isomorphism and commute with all induced lattice operators. Combine with F001 to obtain both tensor identifications asserted in the output.

Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb using N004. The family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R by N004, using iota from N002. Define beta_i to be its reduced image in V_K through F001. Scalar extension of its coordinate maps gives a K-basis: every pure tensor has its finite coordinate expansion in beta_i, and the extended coordinate maps take beta_i to the corresponding coordinate unit vectors, proving independence. Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. Applying N001 to b e_i and using the tensor isomorphisms gives x beta_0=0, x beta_i=(λ−i+1)beta_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<λ, y beta_λ=0; h beta_i=(λ−2i)beta_i. All coefficients are the integer images in K. This proves the required basis and its generator matrices.
For each r∈I, r≤λ

Choose the basis beta supplied by N005 and define T by its displayed formula. Let W⊆V_K be any K-linear subspace. Assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. Closure under x,y implies closure under their nonnegative powers. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. A linear subspace is closed under scalar multiplication and compositions of preserving maps, so W is invariant under every T_ij.
In the zero case temporarily assume L2: W={0}. Then the desired disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately. Discharge L2 to obtain the implication for this case.

For the other case assume L3: W≠{0}. A nonzero subspace contains a nonzero vector, and the beta basis of N005 expands any such vector uniquely. Its coefficients cannot all be zero. Thus there exist a vector w∈W, a coefficient family c∈K^I and an index j∈I with w=∑_{k∈I}c_k beta_k, w≠0 and c_j≠0. Record this compatible joint existence before choosing the witnesses.

Choose compatible w,c,j as in F003. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit action of N005 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. By F001 this vector belongs to W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives beta_i∈W. This holds for every i; since beta is a K-basis, W=V_K. No chosen vector or coordinate is present in that conclusion. Discharge L3 to obtain: if W≠{0}, then W=V_K.

Classical case elimination on W={0} or W≠{0}, using F002 and F004, gives W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W: every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V_K. N005 also gives dim_K V_K=λ+1>0, so V_K is nonzero. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.

52:     (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=

124:   ∀ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →

135: def CommonModule (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)

137:   (∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v) ∧

142:   Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧
143:   (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧

145:   Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) = 1

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
