import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
abbrev Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)


def Lowering (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℕ,
    h ((y ^ t) v) = (((lam - 2 * (t : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
    x ((y ^ (t + 1)) v) =
      (((((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (lam - (t : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v)
def CoordinateCore (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∃ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, lam.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h
def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ((lam.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = lam + 1 ∧
  0 < lam.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Index lam) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
  Lowering lam x y h v ∧
  (∀ i : Index lam, e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧
  CoordinateCore lam x y h v ∧
  DividedFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) (divided x) (divided y)
def LocalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  (iota p M).range = Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V) ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (localizedImage p M : Set V) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ r, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r) ∧
    RPreserves p M (divided x r) ∧ RPreserves p M (divided y r)) ∧
  Preserves M x ∧ Preserves M y ∧ Preserves M h ∧
  RPreserves p M x ∧ RPreserves p M y ∧ RPreserves p M h ∧
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a
def MatrixIdentities (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Index lam,
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    divided x (lam.toNat - i.val) * (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b i (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) * divided y (lam.toNat - j.val) =
      (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℂ) • E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) j ∧
    (∃ c : R p, (c : ℚ) = (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℚ) ∧ IsUnit c) ∧
    E lam b i j = MatrixWord lam (divided x) (divided y) i j ∧
    RPreserves p M (E lam b i j)
def CommonModule (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v) ∧
  Nontrivial (J p M y v) ∧ Module.Finite (R p) (J p M y v) ∧
  ∃ c : (Index lam → J p M y v) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M,
    ∀ g, iota p M (c g) = ∑ i : Index lam, (g i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def RationalLine (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧
  (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧
  Module.Finite ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) = 1
def PrincipalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  RationalLine p M y v ∧ (∃ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b) ∧
  ∀ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b → BasisLift p lam M y v b
def TensorMaps (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (hp : CharP K p) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (kap : R p →+* K) : Prop :=
  letI : CharP K p := hp
  letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
    (psi : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), psi (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) =
      c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (ModN.mkQ p u)) ∧
    (∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M) (z : VK K M),
      phi (f.baseChange K z) = (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K (phi z)) ∧
    (∀ f : Module.End (R p) (MR p M),
      ∃ fbar : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
        (∀ u, fbar (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f u)) ∧
        ∀ z, psi (f.baseChange K z) = fbar.baseChange K (psi z))
def ScalarReduction (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (hp : CharP K p) (kap : R p →+* K),
    (∀ (r : R p) (a b : ℤ), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ) → kap r = (a : K) / (b : K)) ∧
    TensorMaps p K hp M kap
def ReducedBasis (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
  ∃ (beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M)) (b : ℂ),
    Principal p M y v b ∧
    (∃ (kap : R p →+* K),
      letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
      ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
        (c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)),
        (∀ (s : K) (m : M), phi (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
        (∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val) ∧
        ∀ i, phi (beta i) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R p] (c i)) ∧
    Module.finrank K (VK K M) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
    GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)
def ReducedUnits (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ j : Index lam, (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
    (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat →
      (a.X r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.x.baseChange K) ^ r ∧
      (a.Y r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.y.baseChange K) ^ r) ∧
    ∀ beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M),
      GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K) →
      ∀ i j k : Index lam,
        MatrixWord lam (fun r => (a.X r).baseChange K) (fun r => (a.Y r).baseChange K) i j (beta k) =
          if j = k then beta i else 0

end SL2Reduction

52:     (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=

62:     (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=

65:     (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
66:   ∀ i : Index lam,
67:     x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
68:       (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
69:     y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
70:     h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)

72:     (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
73:   ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
74:     X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
75:       ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
76:       else 0) ∧

83:     (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))

96:   ∀ t : ℕ,

99:       (((((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (lam - (t : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v)

101:   (∃ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
102:   (∀ t : ℕ, lam.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
103:   GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h

106:   0 < lam.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Index lam) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
107:   Lowering lam x y h v ∧

results.value: V is an arbitrary complex vector space and x,y,h are its complex-linear Chevalley actions. H003 retains finite dimension, all three commutators, a highest vector of weight λ and irreducibility under the generating actions; this is the operator presentation of the given sl₂-module, with the specified v retained separately in H004. λ remains an integer. Under H002, Index λ = Fin(λ.toNat+1) identifies bijectively with {i∈ℤ | 0≤i≤λ}; natural differences are used only inside this range. M is a ℤ-submodule of V; H005 supplies an arbitrary integer basis that is also a complex basis, and stability under every divided power. R is the ℤ-subalgebra of ℚ generated by the displayed prime-to-p fractions, with its exact original carrier established by T005; it is not assumed to be the whole ℚ. MR=R⊗ℤM and iota is the actual scalar multiplication lift; identifying with its image is justified only by N002. J_i and J are preimages of that image under c↦c e_i. qmul is the actual multiplication map ℚ⊗R J→ℂ. Scalar-first VK=K⊗ℤM is the same source tensor construction with factors swapped; T014 uses this convention throughout. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the image of multiplication by p. LatticeOps carries the actual restrictions, and Agrees specifies each value, rather than adding any action assumption. The target constructs these unique restrictions and states nonzero VK and every K-submodule invariant under x,y,h is bottom or top. Proposition-valued definitions only package displayed obligations; none proves them. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, integer coefficients are cast to the indicated field, and all factorials/choose arguments are natural numbers. Inspected pinned APIs: CharP K p asserts exactly (n:K)=0 iff p divides n, rather than merely p·1=0. Module.End multiplication is f.comp g, and Basis.coord is the coefficient function from its finitely-supported coordinate equivalence. LinearMap.liftBaseChange sends s⊗m to s•f(m), while LinearMap.baseChange sends s⊗m to s⊗f(m). ModN is the quotient by the range of the integer-linear p-multiplication map and its ZMod-module instance is canonical. ZMod.algebra is explicitly installed under CharP; the R-action on K is explicitly the one supplied by κ.toAlgebra. Scalar towers for R⊂ℚ⊂ℂ and R⊂ℂ acting on V use those actual inclusion maps. The two finrank theorems require strong rank condition; here R is a subring of ℚ and ℚ is a field, so these are consequences, not extra parameters.

argument.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary i∈I.
Fix arbitrary j∈I.
Let c be an arbitrary complex scalar when testing membership in J_j.
Let u∈M_R be arbitrary.
Choose the coordinates d of iota(u) in the e basis, iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k.

argument.text: By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

produces.statement: For every i0∈I, J_i0=J, and E_i0i0 maps iota(M_R) onto J e_i0.

argument.text: For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

produces.statement: The coordinate sum map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear isomorphism; M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k under iota.

argument.text: By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

11: 
12: /-!
13: # Quotienting out a free `ℤ`-module
14: 
15: If `G` is a rank `d` free `ℤ`-module, then `G/nG` is a finite group of cardinality `n ^ d`.
16: -/
17: 
18: @[expose] public section
19: 
20: open Finsupp Function Module
21: 
22: variable {G H M : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {n : ℕ}
23: 
24: variable (G n) in
25: /-- `ModN G n` denotes the quotient of `G` by multiples of `n` -/
26: abbrev ModN : Type _ := G ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
27: 
28: namespace ModN
29: 
30: instance : Module (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := QuotientAddGroup.zmodModule (by simp)
31: 
32: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
33: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of monoids: Monoid homomorphisms from `ModN G n`
34: are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
35: protected def liftEquiv [AddMonoid M] : (ModN G n →+ M) ≃ {φ : G →+ M // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} where
36:   toFun f := ⟨f.comp (QuotientAddGroup.mk' _), fun g ↦ by
37:     let Gn : AddSubgroup G := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).toAddSubgroup
38:     suffices n • g ∈ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn).ker by
39:       simp only [AddMonoidHom.coe_comp, comp_apply, ← map_nsmul]
40:       change f (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn (n • g)) = 0 -- Can we avoid `change`?
41:       rw [this, map_zero]
42:     simp [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk', Gn]⟩
43:   invFun φ := QuotientAddGroup.lift _ φ <| by rintro - ⟨g, rfl⟩; simpa using φ.property g
44:   left_inv f := by
45:     ext x
46:     induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on
47:     rfl -- Should `simp` suffice here?
48:   right_inv φ := by aesop
49: 
50: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of `ZMod n`-modules: `ZMod n`-linear maps from
51: `ModN G n` are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
52: protected def liftEquiv' [AddCommGroup H] [Module (ZMod n) H] :
53:     (ModN G n →ₗ[ZMod n] H) ≃ {φ : G →+ H // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} :=
54:   (AddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMapEquiv n).symm.toEquiv.trans ModN.liftEquiv
55: 
56: variable (n) in
57: /-- The quotient map `G → G / nG`. -/
58: def mkQ : G →+ ModN G n := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).mkQ
59: 
60: variable [NeZero n]
61: 
62: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
63: /-- Given a free module `G` over `ℤ`, construct the corresponding basis
64: of `G / ⟨n⟩` over `ℤ / nℤ`. -/
65: noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) : Basis ι (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := by
66:   set ψ : G →+ G := zsmulAddGroupHom n
67:   set nG := LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
68:   set H := G ⧸ nG
69:   set φ : G →ₗ[ℤ] H := nG.mkQ
70:   let mod : (ι →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := mapRange.linearMap (Int.castAddHom _).toIntLinearMap
71:   let f : G →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ℤ) := b.repr
72:   have hker : nG ≤ LinearMap.ker (mod.comp f) := by
73:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
74:     ext b
75:     simp [mod, f]
76:   let g : H →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := nG.liftQ (mod.comp f) hker
77:   refine ⟨.ofBijective (g.toAddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMap n) ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
78:   · rw [AddMonoidHom.coe_toZModLinearMap, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe, injective_iff_map_eq_zero,
79:       nG.mkQ_surjective.forall]
80:     intro x hx
81:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply, g] at hx
82:     rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply] at hx
83:     replace hx : ∀ b, ↑n ∣ f x b := by
84:       simpa [mod, DFunLike.ext_iff, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using! hx
85:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply]
86:     rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
87:     choose c hc using hx
88:     refine ⟨b.repr.symm ⟨(f x).support, c, by simp [hc, NeZero.ne]⟩, b.repr.injective ?_⟩
89:     simpa [DFunLike.ext_iff, eq_comm] using! hc
90:   · suffices mod ∘ b.repr = g ∘ nG.mkQ by
91:       exact (this ▸ (mapRange_surjective _ (map_zero _) ZMod.intCast_surjective).comp
92:         b.repr.surjective).of_comp
93:     ext x b
94:     simp [mod, g, f, H]
95: 
96: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
97: lemma basis_apply_eq_mkQ {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) (i : ι) : basis b i = mkQ n (b i) := by
98:   rw [Basis.apply_eq_iff]; simp [basis, mkQ]
99: 
100: variable [Module.Free ℤ G] [Module.Finite ℤ G]
101: 
102: instance instModuleFinite : Module.Finite (ZMod n) (ModN G n) :=
103:   .of_basis <| basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G
104: 
105: instance instFinite : Finite (ModN G n) := Module.finite_of_finite (ZMod n)
106: 
107: variable (G n)
108: @[simp] lemma natCard_eq : Nat.card (ModN G n) = n ^ Module.finrank ℤ G := by
109:   simp [Nat.card_congr (basis <| Module.Free.chooseBasis ℤ G).repr.toEquiv,
110:     Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Module.finrank_eq_card_chooseBasisIndex]
111: 
112: end ModN

20: ## Main declarations
21: 
22: - `Algebra.TensorProduct.semiring`: the ring structure on `A ⊗[R] B` for two `R`-algebras `A`, `B`.
23: - `Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra`: the `S`-algebra structure on `A ⊗[R] B`, for when `A` is
24:   additionally an `S` algebra.
25: 
26: ## References
27: 
28: * [C. Kassel, *Quantum Groups* (§II.4)][Kassel1995]
29: 
30: -/
31: 
32: @[expose] public section
33: 
34: assert_not_exists Equiv.Perm.cycleType
35: 
36: open scoped TensorProduct
37: 
38: open TensorProduct
39: 
40: 
41: namespace LinearMap
42: 
43: section liftBaseChange
44: 
45: variable {R M N} (A) [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid M]
46: variable [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module A N] [IsScalarTower R A N]
47: 
48: /--
49: If `M` is an `R`-module and `N` is an `A`-module, then `A`-linear maps `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N`
50: correspond to `R` linear maps `M →ₗ[R] N` by composing with `M → A ⊗ M`, `x ↦ 1 ⊗ x`.
51: -/
52: def liftBaseChangeEquiv : (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N) :=
53:   (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf _ _ _).symm.trans (AlgebraTensorModule.lift.equiv _ _ _ _ _ _)
54: 
55: /-- If `N` is an `A` module, we may lift a linear map `M →ₗ[R] N` to `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N` -/
56: abbrev liftBaseChange (l : M →ₗ[R] N) : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N :=
57:   LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv A l
58: 
59: @[simp]
60: lemma liftBaseChange_tmul (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (x y) : l.liftBaseChange A (x ⊗ₜ y) = x • l y := rfl
61: 
62: lemma liftBaseChange_one_tmul (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (y) : l.liftBaseChange A (1 ⊗ₜ y) = l y := by simp
63: 
64: @[simp]
65: lemma liftBaseChangeEquiv_symm_apply (l : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N) (x) :
66:     (liftBaseChangeEquiv A).symm l x = l (1 ⊗ₜ x) := rfl
67: 
68: lemma liftBaseChange_comp {P} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module A P] [Module R P] [IsScalarTower R A P]
69:     (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (l' : N →ₗ[A] P) :
70:       l' ∘ₗ l.liftBaseChange A = (l'.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ l).liftBaseChange A := by
71:   ext
72:   simp
73: 
74: @[simp]
75: lemma range_liftBaseChange (l : M →ₗ[R] N) :
76:     LinearMap.range (l.liftBaseChange A) = Submodule.span A (LinearMap.range l) := by
77:   apply le_antisymm
78:   · rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
79:     induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on
80:     · simp
81:     · rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul]
82:       exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨_, rfl⟩)
83:     · rw [map_add]
84:       exact add_mem ‹_› ‹_›
85:   · rw [Submodule.span_le]
86:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
87:     exact ⟨1 ⊗ₜ x, by simp⟩
88: 
89: end liftBaseChange
90: 
91: end LinearMap

argument.text: By H001, every integer prime to p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. The formula defining kappa:R→K is independent of fractional representatives by cross multiplication, preserves addition and multiplication, and extends the integer map. The balanced tensor maps V_K=M⊗_ℤ K→M_R⊗_R K and back are m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c and (s⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗kappa(s)c. The tensor relations show that both are well-defined; the two composites fix pure tensors, hence are identity maps. Thus they are inverse K-linear isomorphisms. Since the maps act only on scalar factors, they intertwine every operator preserving M, including x,y,h,X_r,Y_r by N002.

argument.text: The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module. The maps M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K and back send u⊗c to [u]⊗c and [u]⊗c to u⊗c. Changing u by a multiple of p changes u⊗c by zero, since p=0 in K. These formulas are balanced for the quotient R-action, are independent of representatives, and are inverse on pure tensors. They give the second K-linear isomorphism and commute with all induced lattice operators. Combine with F001 to obtain both tensor identifications asserted in the output.

Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. value.justification: The elementary exchange argument bounds the size of any independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: insert independent vectors successively into a spanning list, each time replacing a vector with nonzero coefficient in an expansion, preserving spanning. If an independent family of size dim W did not span, adjoining a vector outside its span would give an independent family of size dim W+1, contradicting that bound applied to a basis of W. Thus the given family spans and is a basis.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. R001.fact: In a finite-dimensional vector space W over a field, a linearly independent family indexed by a finite set J with |J|=dim W is a basis.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space of finite dimension λ+1.
F001 gives |I|=n=λ+1.
Before the dimension step, the displayed polynomial calculation proves linear independence of (e_i).

R001.justification: The elementary exchange argument bounds the size of any independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: insert independent vectors successively into a spanning list, each time replacing a vector with nonzero coefficient in an expansion, preserving spanning.
